findings.issue: Cell 4 emits a live `[style] column 'P_over_N' varies but is not in style.HPARAM_COLUMNS: its values are being AVERAGED OVER. Add it there if it is a hyperparameter, or to PROVENANCE_COLUMNS if it is not.` -- the one warning ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1's acceptance criterion and this gate name explicitly, and the only [style] hit in all 23 notebooks. It fires because the cell assigns `b['P_over_N'] = P[tag] / b['n_data']` onto the arm table and then passes that same frame to `rf.rank_table(b, 'n_data')`, which re-groups it. The numbers are NOT wrong -- P_over_N is a deterministic function of the n_data the grouping already keys on, so nothing meaningful is averaged -- but the banner is what the gate forbids, and it trains readers to ignore a warning that does mean something elsewhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the ranks before adding the derived column: call `ranks[tag] = rf.rank_table(b, 'n_data')` first, then assign `b['P_over_N']` and `ranks[tag]['P_over_N']`; or pass `rf.rank_table(b.drop(columns=['P_over_N']), 'n_data')`. Re-execute and confirm the warning is gone.
